headline: Committee defers possible County purchase of Maui Land and Pine water assets

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: The committee discussed the possible County purchase of Maui Land and Pine water systems in West Maui and Upcountry, and the chair deferred the item until the administration has reports a member requested. The Council must approve any final purchase.
meeting.recap: The only item was the possible County purchase of Maui Land and Pine water assets in West Maui and Upcountry.[[0:11:12]] On May 18, 2026, the mayor announced a memorandum of understanding (MOU, a written outline of basic terms) with the company.[[0:11:57]] The managing director said these and other purchases would raise public control of West Maui drinking water systems from about 45% to 93%.[[0:15:21]] The administration plans to bring the Council an offer and resolution after reviews and appraisals.[[0:25:14]] A testifier supported removing private companies from owning public trust water but raised concerns about water credits.[[0:43:43]] The managing director said the Council must approve any final purchase.[[1:07:05]] The chair deferred the item with no objections until the administration has the reports a member requested.[[2:53:57]]
meeting.next: The County will do due diligence, title reports and appraisals before bringing an offer and resolution to the Council. A question about eminent domain was set aside for a possible later executive session (a closed-door discussion). The item will come back after the administration has and reviews the reports a member requested.

moments.q: "Council would have to approve the ultimate authority to acquire"

issues.oneLine: The County is negotiating to buy Maui Land and Pine water systems in West Maui and Upcountry.
issues.why: The managing director said the goal is long-term water care for future generations facing climate change and drought.

deadlines.t: Recommendations brought back to the Council.

issues.next: Due diligence, title reports and appraisals come before an offer goes to the Council.
issues.brief: The County also wants land to build a 100 million gallon reservoir.[[#1]] An official said the County would not give water credits to golf courses.[[#2]] An official said new water uses will still need a state water use permit after the County buys the assets.[[#3]]
